beats.text: Five short books that quietly rearrange how you think.
One. Meditations by Marcus Aurelius — a Roman emperor's private notes on staying sane.
Two. Letters from a Stoic by Seneca — the wisest advice you'll ever get from two thousand years away.
Three. The Myth of Sisyphus by Camus — how to find meaning in a world that offers none.
Four. Man's Search for Meaning by Viktor Frankl — purpose, forged in the darkest place imaginable.
Five. The Tao Te Ching by Lao Tzu — eighty short verses on doing more by forcing less.
Five books. A single weekend each. And a different pair of eyes by the end.
